mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of periods following a 0.3pp UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% year-over-year signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of cases following a 5% YoY increase in HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 4.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and slowing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS slows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strong supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of cases following a 1% MoM increase in INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 2% annualized signals weakening demand, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 growth is below 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strong demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of cases following a 2% MoM increase in RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.
